To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a DNA vaccine expressing measles virus hemagglutiniin induces long-lived high-avidity neutralizing Abs in neonatal mice, even in the presence of maternally derived measles antibodies.

neonatal immunization by Sindbis virus-based DNA vaccines encoding either MV-H or H+F glycoproteins induces adult-like measles immunity in the presence of maternal Ab, including neutralizing Abs, syncytium-inhibiting Abs, IgG secreting cells, and Th1 type cell mediated immunity.
Sindbis virus-based DNA vaccines can induce long-lasting neutralizing and cell-mediated immunity in the presence of maternal antibodies in neonatal mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a vaccine to protect against measles in the first year of life.
understanding the molecular and cellular basis of immune responses to measles vaccine in the neonate, and with the development of a novel approach for the prevention of measles in infants.
developing a vaccine that can protect infants from measles in spite of the presence of maternal antibodies, which interfere with the efficacy of the current measles vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

neonatal vaccination with a DNA vaccine based on the Sindbis virus replicons encoding MV H and F proteins induces robust and long-lasting MV neutralizing Abs and Th1 type cell mediated immunity in the presence of high concentrations of maternal antibodies.
a DNA vaccine can be a promising approach to overcome maternal antibodies and induce a robust immune response in newborns.

neonatal mice born from naive and measles-immunized mothers respond to a measles DNA vaccine with robust neutralizing Ab and cell-mediated immunity that surpasses that elicited by a live attenuated measles virus vaccine in adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a measles DNA vaccine can be given at birth to protect against measles.

neonatal vaccination with a measles DNA vaccine can induce robust humoral immunity and cell-mediated immunity, and that this response can be further enhanced by boosting with a live attenuated measles virus vaccine.

a measles DNA vaccine can induce adult-like neutralizing antibodies and T-cell responses in the presence of maternal antibodies and that the vaccine can be used to prime for a heterologous measles vaccine.
The main takeaway from our work is that

neonatal immunization against measles with a Sindbis virus replicons-based DNA vaccine induces long lasting, high avidity MV PRN Abs and Th1 cell mediated immunity that surpasses that of adults in the presence of maternal antibodies.
the Sindbis virus replicons are very potent at eliciting protective immune responses against measles in neonates.
a measles DNA vaccine can be used to overcome the problem of maternal antibodies that inhibit the response to the live attenuating vaccine.
